blocks.tamil_translation: “Ya Rasulallah! I fear that my tongue will make me enter Jahannam,” I said. “If so, then where has Istighfar gone?” (Do you not do Istighfar (seeking forgiveness), which can set your tongue right?) I myself do Istighfar a hundred times a day,” the Prophet ﷺ replied.

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ عَدِيِّ بْنِ حَاتِمٍ ﵁ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُوْلُ اللهِ ﷺ: اَيْمَنُ امْرِئئٍ وَاَشْأَمُهُ مَا بَيْنَ لَحْيَيْهِ.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه الطبراني ورجاله رجال الصحيح، مجمع الزوائد:١٠ /٥٣٨
blocks.tamil_translation: “A man's good fortune and misfortune lie between his two jaws (using the tongue properly is a cause of good fortune, and using it improperly is a cause of misfortune),” Hazrat Adi ibn Hatim (RA) narrates that the Prophet ﷺ said.

blocks.arabic_text: عَنِ الْحَسَنِ رَحِمَهُ اللهُ يَقُوْلُ: بَلَغَنَا اَنَّ رَسُوْلَ اللهِ ﷺ قَالَ: رَحِمَ اللهُ عَبْدًا تَكَلَّمَ فَغَنِمَ اَوْ سَكَتَ فَسَلِمَ.
blocks.tamil_translation: “May Allah Ta'ala have mercy on the servant who speaks good words and attains their benefit in this world and the Hereafter, or who stays silent and protects himself from the evils of the tongue!” — this hadith of Rasulullah ﷺ has reached us,' Hazrat Hasan (RH) narrates.

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو ﵄ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُوْلُ اللهِ ﷺ: مَنْ صَمَتَ نَجَا.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه الترمذي وقال: هذا حديث غريب، باب حديث من كان يؤمن بالله...، رقم:٢٥٠١
